{{nihongo|'''Shima Shrine'''|志磨神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

'''Shima Shrine'' (Shima Shrine) is located in {{ill|Wakayama Prefecture|Q131314|qid=Q131314}}{{ill|Wakayama (city)|ar|واكاياما (واكاياما)|arz|واكاياما|az|Vakayama|azb|واکایاما (شهر)|ban|Wakayama, Wakayama|be|Вакаяма (горад)|bg|Вакаяма (град)|ca|Wakayama|ce|Вакаяма (гӀала)|ceb|Wakayama Shi|cs|Wakajama|cy|Wakayama|de|Wakayama|eo|Vakajamo|es|Wakayama|et|Wakayama|eu|Wakayama|fa|واکایاما (شهر)|fi|Wakayama|fr|Wakayama|ga|Wakayama|gl|Wakayama|he|וקאיאמה|hy|Վակայամա|id|Wakayama, Wakayama|it|Wakayama|ja|和歌山市|kaa|Vakayama|ko|와카야마시|ky|Вакаяма|lt|Vakajama|mzn|واکایاما (شهر)|nl|Wakayama (stad)|no|Wakayama (Wakayama)|os|Вакаямæ (сахар)|pl|Wakayama|pt|Wakayama (cidade)|ro|Wakayama|ru|Вакаяма (город)|sc|Wakayama|sh|Wakayama|simple|Wakayama (city)|sr|Вакајама|sv|Wakayama|sw|Wakayama, Wakayama|szl|Wakayama|tg|Вакаяма|th|วากายามะ (เมือง)|tl|Lungsod ng Wakayama|tr|Wakayama|tt|Вакаяма (шәһәр)|tum|Wakayama|uk|Вакаяма|ur|واکایاما، واکایاما|uz|Vakayama|vi|Wakayama (thành phố)|war|Wakayama (syudad)|wuu|和歌山市|zh|和歌山市|zh_classical|和歌山市|zh_min_nan|Wakayama-chhī|zh_yue|和歌山市|qid=Q200747}}{{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}. {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}) and {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}}.

{{ill|Itate Shrine|ja|伊達神社 (和歌山市)|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City), {{ill|Shizuhi Shrine|ja|静火神社|qid=Q28693031}} (Wada, Wakayama City, {{jal ink|Kamayama Shrine|Q11597743}}Setssha) is called ``Kinosanshoshya''{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

== Enshrined God ==
The following two deities are enshrined.<ref>The notation and pronunciation of the enshrined deities are based on the shrine history book and the explanation board within the precincts. </ref>.
; Main enshrined deity
:* '''Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto'' (Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto) - Another name is {{ill|Ichikishima-hime|fr|Ichikishimahime|ja|イチキシマヒメ|simple|Ichikishima-hime|zh|市寸島比賣命|qid=Q11059454|lt=Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto}} (Ichikishima Hime no Mikoto).
; Deity enshrined
:* Ikudama no Kami - The history of his enshrinement is unknown {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1987}}.

As a different theory, ``{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}'' states that ``Kisansho Shrine'' enshrines the three deities of Idakeso (Itake no Mikoto, Oyatsuhime no Mikoto, and Tomatsuhime no Mikoto), and assumes that the deity enshrined at Shima Shrine is Oyatsuhime no Mikoto {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. However, since Shima Shrine is located on Kawanakajima in {{ill|Kinokawa River|Q1042624|qid=Q1042624}}, Nakatsushima Hime no Mikoto is appropriate from the location point of view {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

Also, in "{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}," Funatama Shrine in the {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} Setsusha is said to be the deity of the Ki clan and the headquarters of ``Shima-kami, Shizuka-kami, and Date-kami'' {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}.

== History ==
Our company was designated and renamed Shima Shrine "Shima Shrine" in the {{ill|Genna|Q635245|qid=Q635245|lt=Genna}} years ({{ill|1615|Q6784|qid=Q6784}}-{{ill|1624|Q6821|qid=Q6821}}) {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. Currently, as the place name ``{{ill|Nakanoshima|Q17226981|qid=Q17226981|lt=Nakanoshima}}'' indicates, it is located on an island in the {{ill|Kinokawa River|Q1042624|qid=Q1042624}} delta, but the company name ``Shima'' is said to refer to Kawanakajima.{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. Before Hiden, our company was called ``Kuzu Myojin (Kunizu Myojin),'' and at the time of the Genna era, there were six small shrines on the island, including our company, but Kuzu Myojin was chosen because it had the best location.{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}

== Outline ==
In ancient literature, in the ``{{ill|Shinshō Kyakuchokufushō|Q11502312|qid=Q11502312}}'' {{ill|Daidō|Q1373191|qid=Q1373191|lt=Daido}} 1st year ({{ill|806|Q30021|qid=Q30021}}), {{ill|Kanbe (social class)|Q11589711|qid=Q11589711|lt=Kobe}} was the name of the island god. There is a description of ``Seven Houses'' {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The existence of Kobe can also be seen in the mention of "Island Kobe" in Nagusa District in "{{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}" {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}<ref group="Note">Among the Kisansho shrines, Shimagami is the only one where Kobe is mentioned. {{Harv|Shima Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1987}}. </ref>. In national history, it is known as ``Shima-kami'' along with Date-kami and Shizuka-kami. (Japan)|Q1075605|Jōwa}} In 11 years ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}), he was given the lower rank of Seigoi, and in {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}}3 years ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}) he was given the rank of junior fourth rank and lower. (Japan)|Q1075635|Jōgan}} In the 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), he was promoted to Seishiinoge, Jogan 17th year ({{jalink|875|Q {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}} which contains an article about the promotion of Junior Third Rank (Junior Third Rank|Q11591025}}).{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=extended}} "{{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448}}" established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) {{jali nk|Engishiki Shrine Name Book|Q11064932|Shin Name Book}}, {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053}}{{ill|Nagusa district|Q11415547|qid=Q11415547}} "Shima Shrine" In addition to being listed as ``Meishin University'' and listed in {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}, it is also listed as ``Shoichii Shima Okami'' in ``{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}''{{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.Also, Shima Shrine is {{ill|Itate Shrine|ja|伊達神社 (和歌山市)|qid=Q11380847|lt=Date Shrine}} (Sonobe, Wakayama City), {{ill|Shizuhi Shrine|ja|静火神社|qid=Q28693031}} (Wada, Wakayama City), and is said to have been called "Kinosanshoshya" {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. The description of "Kisanshosha" is found in the storage rice book of {{ill|Eishō (Heian period)|Q1193549|qid=Q1193549}}3 ({{ill|1048|Q19359|qid=Q19359}}), as well as in "{{ill|Chūyūki|Q11363231|qid=Q11363231}}" ink|Tennin|Q1193599}} 2nd year ({{ill|1109|Q19515|qid=Q19515}}), "{{ill|Ryōjin Hishō|Q3010584|qid=Q3010584}}" appears to be a four-phrase divine poem {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}. In "{{ill|Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine Chronicles|Q11381815|qid=Q11381815}}", about the origin of Kisansho Shrine, {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} {{jalink|Sankan Conquest} It is said that {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}} was enshrined in {{ill|Takenouchi no Sukune|Q1073668|qid=Q1073668}} for the three ships used in the raid|Q11249435}}.The location of the ``Shima Shrine'' mentioned in the above documents was later unknown, but it was identified in the Genwa period ({{ill|1615|Q6784|qid=Q6784}}-{{ill|1624|Q6821|qid=Q6821}}) to our company, which was then called ``Kuzu (Kunizu) Myojin'' {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Gods)|1986}}. According to "{{ill|Kii Zoku Fudoki|Q11604964|qid=Q11604964}}," our company was established for {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} years ({{ill|1596|Q6785|qid=Q6785}}-{{ill|1615|Q6784|qid=Q6784}}) It used to have five fields of rice fields as its shrine territory, but it was confiscated during land survey, and then it was rebuilt by the {{ill|Kishū Tokugawa family|Q11605046|qid=Q11605046}} {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Heibonsha)|1983}}.

After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}17 ({{ill|1942|Q18625|qid=Q18625}}) In {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was promoted to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Prefectural shrine}} in {{Sfn|Shima Shrine (Shikiuchi shrine)|1987}}.

== God level ==
* Records of {{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|Q11591025|qid=Q11591025}} dedication in the history of the Six Kingdoms
** {{ill|Jōwa (Heian period)|Q1075605|qid=Q1075605|lt=Jōwa}} November 3, 11 years ({{ill|844|Q23835|qid=Q23835}}), from the lower junior fifth rank to the lower upper fifth rank (``{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|Q1041301|qid=Q1041301}}'') - The notation is ``Shima God''.
** October 21, 3rd year of {{ill|Kashō|Q1373157|qid=Q1373157}} ({{ill|850|Q30364|qid=Q30364}}), Junior Fourth Rank Lower (``{{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|Q1052905|qid=Q1052905}}'') - Written as ``Shima God''.
** {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jogan}} January 27, 1st year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from the lower rank of the fourth rank to the lower rank of the fourth rank (``{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}'') - The notation is ``Shima God''.
** October 17, 17th year of Jogan ({{ill|875|Q23816|qid=Q23816}}), from the upper fourth rank to the third rank of junior rank (``Nihon Sandai Jirroku'') - Written as ``Shima no Kami.''
* After Six Kingdoms History
** Shoichii (``{{ill|Kii no Kuni Jinmyō-chō|Q17210008|qid=Q17210008}}'') - Written as ``Shima Okami''.

== Festival ==
The main festivals are as follows. <ref> Festival descriptions are from [http://wakayama-jinjacho.or.jp/jdb/sys/user/GetWjtTbl.php?JinjyaNo=1032 Shima Shrine] (Wakayama Prefectural Shrine Agency). </ref>.
* Star Festival Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Summer Festival (Yoimiya July 14th, Hongu Shrine July 15th)
*Children's mikoshi togyo (2nd Saturday of July)
* Annual festival (October 15th)
* Niwakuri ritual (night of December 15th)
